verses.text: King David was now very old. His servants covered him with blankets, but he could not keep warm.

So his servants said to him, "Let us look for a young unmarried woman for our lord the king. She can wait on the king and take care of him. She can lie beside you, so that our lord the king will keep warm."
So they searched all over Israel for a beautiful young woman. They found Abishag from Shunem and brought her to the king.
The young woman was very beautiful. She took care of the king and served him, but the king did not have sex with her.
Now Adonijah, the son of David's wife Haggith, began to make himself important. He said, "I will be king." So he got chariots and horsemen for himself, and fifty men to run ahead of him.
His father had never once corrected him by asking, "Why are you doing that?" He was also very handsome, and he was born next after Absalom.
Adonijah talked with Joab son of Zeruiah and with Abiathar the priest, and they followed him and helped him.
But Zadok the priest, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, Nathan the prophet, Shimei, Rei, and David's mighty warriors did not join Adonijah.
Adonijah sacrificed sheep, cattle, and fat calves at the Stone of Zoheleth near En Rogel. He invited all his brothers, the king's sons, and all the royal officials from Judah.
But he did not invite Nathan the prophet, Benaiah, the mighty warriors, or his brother Solomon.
Then Nathan said to Bathsheba, Solomon's mother, "Haven't you heard that Adonijah son of Haggith has made himself king, and our lord David doesn't even know about it?
Now let me give you some advice, so that you can save your own life and the life of your son Solomon.

Go in to King David and say to him, 'My lord the king, didn't you promise me with an oath, "Your son Solomon will surely be king after me, and he will sit on my throne"? Then why has Adonijah become king?'
While you are still there talking with the king, I will come in after you and tell him that what you said is true."
So Bathsheba went to see the king in his room. He was very old, and Abishag from Shunem was taking care of him.
Bathsheba bowed down low to show respect to the king. The king asked, "What do you want?"
She said to him, "My lord, you yourself promised me with an oath by the LORD your God, 'Your son Solomon will surely be king after me, and he will sit on my throne.'
But now Adonijah has become king, and you, my lord the king, don't even know about it.
He has sacrificed a great many cattle, fat calves, and sheep. He has invited all the king's sons, Abiathar the priest, and Joab the commander of the army. But he did not invite your servant Solomon.
My lord the king, all Israel is watching you. They are waiting for you to tell them who will sit on your throne after you.
If you don't, then as soon as my lord the king dies and is buried with his ancestors, my son Solomon and I will be treated as criminals."
While she was still speaking with the king, Nathan the prophet arrived.
The king was told, "Nathan the prophet is here." He came in and bowed down in front of the king with his face to the ground.
Nathan said, "My lord the king, did you say, 'Adonijah will be king after me, and he will sit on my throne'?

Today he went down and sacrificed a great many cattle, fat calves, and sheep. He invited all the king's sons, the army commanders, and Abiathar the priest. Right now they are eating and drinking with him and shouting, 'Long live King Adonijah!'
But he did not invite me, your servant, or Zadok the priest, or Benaiah son of Jehoiada, or your servant Solomon.
Has my lord the king done this without telling your servants who should sit on the throne after you?"
Then King David said, "Call Bathsheba in here." So she came in and stood in front of the king.
The king made this promise: "As surely as the LORD lives, who has rescued me from every trouble,

I will do today what I promised you with an oath by the LORD, the God of Israel. I said, 'Your son Solomon will surely be king after me, and he will sit on my throne in my place.' I will certainly do it today."
Then Bathsheba bowed down with her face to the ground to show respect to the king and said, "May my lord King David live forever!"
King David said, "Call in Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah son of Jehoiada." When they came before the king,
he said to them, "Take my officials with you. Put my son Solomon on my own mule and take him down to the Gihon spring.
There Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet must anoint him king over Israel. Blow the trumpet and shout, 'Long live King Solomon!'
Then come back up with him, and he will come and sit on my throne and be king in my place. I have chosen him to be ruler over Israel and Judah."
Benaiah son of Jehoiada answered the king, "Amen! May the LORD, the God of my lord the king, say so too.
Just as the LORD has been with my lord the king, may he be with Solomon. May he make Solomon's throne even greater than the throne of my lord King David!"
So Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and the Kerethites and Pelethites went down. They put Solomon on King David's mule and took him to the Gihon spring.
Zadok the priest took the horn of olive oil from the holy tent and anointed Solomon. Then they blew the trumpet, and all the people shouted, "Long live King Solomon!"
All the people followed him back up, playing flutes and celebrating with great joy. They were so loud that the ground shook with the noise.
Adonijah and all his guests heard the noise just as they were finishing their meal. When Joab heard the sound of the trumpet, he asked, "Why is the city in such an uproar?"
While he was still speaking, Jonathan son of Abiathar the priest arrived. Adonijah said, "Come in. You are a good man, and you must be bringing good news."
Jonathan answered Adonijah, "Not at all! Our lord King David has made Solomon king.
The king sent Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and the Kerethites and Pelethites with him, and they put him on the king's mule.
Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet anointed him king at the Gihon spring. They have come up from there celebrating, and the whole city is ringing with the noise. That is the sound you hear.
What's more, Solomon is now sitting on the royal throne.

The king's officials have also come to congratulate our lord King David. They said, 'May your God make Solomon's name even more famous than yours, and his throne greater than yours!' And the king bowed down in worship on his bed.
The king also said, 'Praise the LORD, the God of Israel! Today he has let my own eyes see one of my sons sitting on my throne.'"
Then all of Adonijah's guests were terrified. They got up and each one went his own way.
Adonijah was afraid of Solomon, so he got up and went and took hold of the horns of the altar.

Then Solomon was told, "Adonijah is afraid of King Solomon. He is holding on to the horns of the altar and saying, 'Let King Solomon first promise me with an oath that he will not kill his servant with the sword.'"
Solomon said, "If he shows himself to be a good man, not one hair of his head will fall to the ground. But if any evil is found in him, he will die."
Then King Solomon sent men, and they brought Adonijah down from the altar. He came and bowed down to King Solomon, and Solomon said to him, "Go home."
